name: Duchess
waitingLines: Oh, dear, I couldn’t possibly leave without seeing {partner}. I’ll put the kettle on.
Oh, dear, I’ll just wait right here for {partner}. These scones won’t eat themselves.

questions.scene: Duchess hesitates, then leans in delicately.
lines: Oh, dear, this one's a bit cheeky. But it's true!
questions.question: Where do badgers go to the toilet?

choices.label: In special pits called latrines
reply: Oh, quite right, darling!
Badgers dig latrine pits, often near the edges of their territory.
They even double as boundary markers. Practical and polite.

choices.label: Right in the bedroom
reply: Oh, dear heavens, NO.
They dig special pits called latrines, away from the sett.
We have standards. Very high standards.

choices.label: In a neighbor's garden
reply: Oh, dear, how rude! Though, occasionally...
They dig latrine pits away from the sett.
Tidy homes, tidy manners.

questions.factBasis: Badgers use dug latrine pits, often at territory boundaries.

questions.scene: Duchess places a rose and an apple side by side, with a knowing smile.
lines: Oh, dear, these two are related. Family secrets.
questions.question: What do roses and apples have in common?

choices.label: They both grow underground
reply: Oh, dear, no.
They're in the same plant family, the rose family.
Along with pears, cherries, and strawberries. A big, sweet family.

choices.label: They're in the same plant family
reply: Oh, splendid! Cousins indeed!
Roses, apples, pears, cherries, and strawberries are all in the rose family.
Bartholomew brings me both on our anniversary. Now I know why.

choices.label: Nothing at all
reply: Oh, dear, they're family!
Roses and apples are both in the rose family.
So an apple is, in a way, a rose's cousin. Lovely.

questions.factBasis: Roses and apples are both in the family Rosaceae.

questions.scene: Duchess pours two cups of tea and slides one to you.
lines: Tea question! My specialty.
questions.question: Black, green, white, and oolong tea all come from what?

choices.label: The same plant: Camellia sinensis
reply: Oh, well done!
It's all how the leaves are dried, rolled, and oxidized.
One plant, many personalities. Like Bartholomew.

choices.label: Different plants for each kind
reply: Oh, dear, it surprises everyone!
They all come from the same plant, Camellia sinensis.
The difference is how the leaves are processed. One plant, many moods.

choices.label: Lavender bushes
reply: Oh, dear, lovely smell, wrong plant.
All true teas come from Camellia sinensis.
Herbal 'teas' like chamomile are technically infusions.

questions.factBasis: Black, green, white and oolong teas come from Camellia sinensis.

questions.scene: Duchess opens a tiny jar of golden-red threads, very carefully.
lines: Oh, dear, this cost more than my hat. Spice question.
questions.question: What is saffron, actually?

choices.label: Ground-up golden rocks
reply: Oh, dear, no rocks in my paella.
It's the dried stigmas of a crocus flower.
Each flower has just three. Hand-picked. Very fancy.

choices.label: Tree sap
reply: Oh, dear, sticky, but no.
It's dried threads from crocus flowers.
Thousands of flowers make a small jar. Worth every penny.

choices.label: The dried thread-like parts of a crocus flower
reply: Oh, well done, dear!
Each flower has just three threads, all picked by hand.
It takes thousands of flowers for a small amount. Precious.

questions.factBasis: Saffron is the dried stigmas of Crocus sativus, three per flower.

questions.scene: Duchess touches a very old wooden table with deep respect.
lines: About things that last. Like my marriage.
questions.question: Bristlecone pines are among the oldest living things. How old can they get?

choices.label: About 100 years
reply: Oh, dear, far older!
Some bristlecone pines are over 4,000 years old.
Older than the pyramids. Puts my wrinkles in perspective.

choices.label: Over 4,000 years
reply: Oh, splendid! Some are older than the pyramids!
One bristlecone pine is estimated at over 4,800 years old.
And I thought forty years was a long time.

choices.label: About 500 years
reply: Oh, dear, keep going!
Some are over 4,800 years old.
Patient, twisty, and still growing. Inspiring.

questions.factBasis: Some Great Basin bristlecone pines exceed 4,800 years.

questions.scene: Duchess shows you a sketch of a badger and a coyote side by side.
lines: An unlikely friendship. My favorite kind.
questions.question: Which animal sometimes hunts alongside American badgers?

choices.label: The swan
reply: Oh, dear, what a picture. But no.
It's the coyote! They sometimes hunt together.
The badger digs, the coyote chases. Very efficient.

choices.label: The coyote
reply: Oh, how thrilling! Yes!
The badger digs underground, the coyote waits above. Teamwork.
An odd couple. The best couples usually are.

choices.label: The house cat
reply: Oh, dear, cats don't share.
It's the coyote. One digs, one chases.
Even wild animals know: teamwork makes the dream work.

questions.factBasis: American badgers and coyotes sometimes hunt cooperatively.

questions.scene: Duchess stirs her tea with a cinnamon stick, smiling.
lines: Oh, dear, my secret ingredient. Do you know where it comes from?
questions.question: What is cinnamon?

choices.label: The inner bark of a tree
reply: Oh, splendid! Bark, indeed!
It curls into sticks as it dries.
Bartholomew thought it grew on bushes. Forty years and he still surprises me.

choices.label: A dried root
reply: Oh, dear, close, but no.
Cinnamon is the inner bark of a tree.
It curls up into quills as it dries.

choices.label: A seed pod
reply: Oh, dear, that's vanilla or cardamom.
Cinnamon is tree bark.
Rolled up and dried. Simple and lovely.

questions.factBasis: Cinnamon is the dried inner bark of Cinnamomum trees.

questions.scene: Duchess stands, bows to you, then does a slow little twirl.
lines: Oh, dear, this one's about a dance that lasts a lifetime.
questions.question: What do Laysan albatross couples do to bond?

choices.label: Build a nest of shiny things
reply: Oh, dear, that's a bowerbird.
Albatrosses do a whole synchronized dance together.
Partners often stay together for life. Lovely.

choices.label: Sing duets at night
reply: Oh, how romantic. Not quite.
They perform an elaborate courtship dance.
Many pairs stay together for decades.

choices.label: A synchronized courtship dance
reply: Oh, yes, darling! Bows, clacks, sky-pointing!
Pairs perform elaborate dances, and many stay together for decades.
Bartholomew and I still dance. Badly. Lovingly.

questions.factBasis: Laysan albatrosses perform synchronized courtship dances; pairs often bond for life.

questions.scene: Duchess holds up an old photo of her and Bartholomew, then a recent one.
lines: Oh, dear, people say old couples start to look alike. Do we?
questions.question: Do long-term couples' faces really grow more alike over time?

choices.label: Yes, they become identical
reply: Oh, dear, Bartholomew has whiskers. I do not.
A large study found no real facial convergence over time.
Couples might just choose similar-looking partners to begin with.

choices.label: Only if they share toothbrushes
reply: Oh, dear! Never!
A large study found no real evidence of faces converging.
We look alike in spirit, darling. Not in snout.

choices.label: A big study found no real evidence of it
reply: Oh, how surprising!
A large 2020 study found couples' faces don't converge over the years.
People may pick partners who look alike from the start. Fancy that.

questions.factBasis: Tea-makorn & Kosinski (2020): no evidence of facial convergence in long-term couples.

questions.scene: Duchess knits a tiny cow-shaped tea cozy and holds it up.
lines: Oh, dear, cows have best friends. I adore this.
questions.question: What did a study find when cows were with their best friends?

choices.label: They mooed louder
reply: Oh, dear, perhaps, but no.
Cows were calmer and less stressed with their favorite buddy.
Friendship is a comfort, darling.

choices.label: They were calmer and less stressed
reply: Oh, how sweet!
Cows showed lower stress when paired with a preferred buddy.
Everyone needs a best friend. Even cows. Even badgers.

choices.label: They ate less
reply: Oh, dear, quite the opposite of stress-eating, but no.
Being with a preferred partner made cows calmer.
Lower heart rates. Happier hearts.

questions.factBasis: McLennan (2013): heifers paired with preferred partners showed reduced stress responses.

questions.scene: Duchess flips through a worn photo album, landing on a café.
lines: Bartholomew and I went here every Friday for 30 years.
questions.question: Date night after years together: the old favorite spot, or somewhere brand new?

choices.label: The old favorite
reply: The old favorite. Oh, how lovely.
Same table, same order, same smile.

choices.label: Somewhere new
reply: Somewhere new. Oh, adventurous!
New memories keep old love young.

A:A: Oh, the old favorite for both of you. How sweet.
Oh, I can just picture it: {partner} and you order without the menu now.
Tradition is a love language, darling.
A:B: Somewhere new for you. {partner} loves the old spot.
Oh, dear, take them somewhere new, then end at the old place for dessert.
Best of both. I've done this. It works.
B:A: The old favorite for you. {partner} wants somewhere new.
Oh, dear, alternate! Odd Fridays old, even Fridays new.
Or try a new dish at the old place. Gentle adventure.
B:B: Oh, somewhere new for both. How exciting!
Darling, you and {partner} are still exploring together. That's the secret.
Bartholomew and I just started trying new places. At 70. Never too late.

questions.scene: Duchess unfolds a yellowed letter tied with ribbon.
lines: This was from Bartholomew. In 1986.
questions.question: Love letters: on paper, or in a text?

choices.label: On paper
reply: On paper. Oh, timeless.
Something to keep in a shoebox forever.

choices.label: In a text
reply: In a text. Oh, modern and quick.
Instant love. My grandcubs approve.

A:A: Paper for both of you. Oh, how romantic.
I'd wager {partner} and you have a box of letters somewhere.
Read them again when you're 80. You'll cry. Happily.
A:B: Texts for you. {partner} prefers paper.
They want something to hold.
Print your favorite text. Hand it over. Sneaky and sweet.
B:A: Paper for you. {partner} prefers texts.
Oh, dear, write them one letter a year. Just one.
They'll pretend it's old-fashioned. They'll keep it forever.
B:B: Texts for both of you. Oh, efficient love.
So you and {partner} probably screenshot the good ones.
My granddaughter says 'that's the new shoebox.' Clever girl.

questions.scene: Duchess strikes a match and lights a small candle on your table.
lines: Oh, dear, keeping the spark alive. After 40 years, I'm an expert.
questions.question: Keeping the spark: weekly date night, little daily surprises, or one big trip a year?

choices.label: Weekly date night
reply: Weekly date night. Oh, reliable romance.
Never let a week go by without each other.

choices.label: Little daily surprises
reply: Daily surprises. Oh, how charming.
A note in a lunchbox, a flower on a pillow.

choices.label: One big trip a year
reply: A big trip. Oh, how grand!
A whole year of looking forward to it.

A:A: Weekly date nights for both. Oh, how steady.
{partner} and you will never run out of Fridays.
Bartholomew and I never skipped one. Except for the flood of '94.
A:B: Daily surprises for you. {partner} prefers a weekly date.
Oh, dear, sneak a surprise into every date night.
They'll never see it coming. Every week.
A:C: Big trip for you. {partner} prefers weekly dates.
Oh, dear, plan the trip on your date nights.
Map out the adventure together. Very romantic.
B:A: Weekly dates for you. {partner} loves daily surprises.
Oh, dear, combine them! A tiny surprise on every date night.
A flower on the table. A note in the menu. Lovely.
B:B: Daily surprises for both. Oh, delightful.
Oh, I can just picture it: you and {partner} are always leaving little notes, aren't you?
Small things, every day. That's the real magic.
B:C: Big trip for you. {partner} loves daily surprises.
Oh, dear, hide trip hints in their daily surprises.
By the end of the year, they'll know where you're going.
C:A: Weekly dates for you. {partner} dreams of a big trip.
Oh, dear, save a little each date night for the big trip.
C:B: Daily surprises for you. {partner} wants a big trip.
Oh, dear, leave clues to the trip in little daily notes.
A treasure hunt to the airport. Charming!
C:C: Big trips for both. Oh, adventurers!
Darling, {partner} and you probably plan the next one on the way home.

questions.scene: Duchess sits in your rocking chair and rocks slowly, smiling at the ceiling.
lines: Let's dream about growing old together.
questions.question: Growing old together: rocking chairs on a porch, or a tiny adventure van?

choices.label: Rocking chairs
reply: Rocking chairs. Oh, I'm with you.
Slow evenings, lemonade, waving at neighbors.

choices.label: Adventure van
reply: Adventure van. Oh, how daring!
Wrinkles and road trips.

A:A: Rocking chairs for both of you. Oh, so peaceful.
I'd wager {partner} and you will wave at every neighbor, every evening.
Bring a blanket. Porches get chilly.
A:B: The van for you. {partner} wants rocking chairs.
Oh, dear, roam first, rock later.
Bring the rocking chairs IN the van. Problem solved.
B:A: Rocking chairs for you. {partner} wants the van.
Oh, dear, take the van to visit porches!
Rock a little, roam a little.
B:B: Adventure van for both. Oh, how bold!
So you and {partner} will be the coolest grandparents ever.
Bartholomew wants one now. Oh, dear.

questions.scene: Duchess hums a waltz and sways slightly in your kitchen.
lines: We still dance, Bartholomew and I.
questions.question: Dancing in the kitchen: constantly, or only on special occasions?

choices.label: Constantly
reply: Constantly. Oh, how wonderful.
Dishes get done slower, but who cares.

choices.label: Only on special occasions
reply: Special occasions. Oh, saving the magic.
Makes it feel extra special.

A:A: You both dance constantly. Oh, how joyful!
{partner} and you probably waltz while the pasta boils.
Never stop. Even when your knees complain.
A:B: Special occasions for you. {partner} dances constantly.
Darling, they're twirling while you're stirring.
Join them once. Just one spin. You'll see.
B:A: You dance constantly. {partner} saves it for special occasions.
Oh, dear, make every Tuesday a special occasion.
They'll catch on. Then join in.
B:B: Special occasions only, both of you. Oh, how sweet.
Oh, I can just picture it: you and {partner} save the magic for birthdays and anniversaries.
When you do dance, it must feel like a movie.

questions.scene: Duchess settles in with tea and a look that says 'story time.'
lines: Oh, dear, every couple has a favorite story.
questions.question: What story does your partner love telling about you two?
questions.selfQuestion: What story do you love telling about you two?

choices.label: How we met
reply: How you met. Oh, the classic.
Every detail, every time.

choices.label: The time something went hilariously wrong
reply: Something hilariously wrong. Oh, the best kind.
Disasters make the best stories.

A:A: How you met, and {partner} knew it.
Oh, they've heard you tell it at every dinner party.
And they still smile. That's love.
A:B: The disaster story for you. {partner} expected how you met.
Oh, dear, they think you're sentimental. You're a comedian.
Tell both. Start sweet, end with the disaster.
B:A: How you met for you. {partner} expected the disaster story.
Well, they think you're all comedy. You're a romantic.
Tell the sweet version tonight.
B:B: The disaster story, and {partner} knew it.
Ha! They've laughed at it a hundred times.
Bartholomew still tells the canoe story. I still blush.

questions.scene: Duchess tucks a quilt over your knees, very gently.
lines: Caring for each other is everything.
questions.question: When you're sick, what would your partner bring you?
questions.selfQuestion: When your partner is sick, what would you bring them?

choices.label: Soup and tea
reply: Soup and tea. Oh, a classic healer.
Warm hands, warm bowls.

choices.label: A stack of comics
reply: Comics. Oh, how fun!
Laughter is medicine.

choices.label: Every blanket in the house
reply: Every blanket. Oh, a nest builder!
Burrito mode, activated.

A:A: Soup and tea, and {partner} knew it.
Oh, they know you'd arrive with a pot of soup and a teapot, both steaming.
Old-fashioned remedies. Bartholomew swears by my leek soup. Swears.
A:B: Comics for you. {partner} guessed soup and tea.
They think you're the serious caretaker.
Laughter first, soup second. A balanced recovery.
A:C: Every blanket for you. {partner} guessed soup and tea.
Darling, they expected a bowl. You brought a blizzard of quilts.
Add one bowl. Make it perfect.
B:A: Soup and tea for you. {partner} guessed comics.
Bless them, they think you're the fun one.
Bring both. Soup in one hand, comics in the other.
B:B: Comics, and {partner} knew it.
Oh, they know you'd prescribe a stack of comics and a silly voice for every character.
Laughter really is medicine, darling. The fun kind.
B:C: Every blanket for you. {partner} guessed comics.
Ha! They expected jokes. You brought warmth.
Read them comics from inside the fort.
C:A: Soup and tea for you. {partner} guessed blankets.
They think you'd smother them in quilts.
You'd smother them in soup. Lovely either way.
C:B: Oh, dear, comics under a blanket fort. Best sick day ever.
They'll recover just to thank you.
C:C: Oh, they know you'll build a fort around them.
Nobody stays cold on your watch.

questions.scene: Duchess hums softly while stirring her tea, then catches herself.
lines: Bartholomew loves when I do that.
questions.question: Which little habit of yours does your partner secretly love?
questions.selfQuestion: Which little habit of your partner's do you secretly love?

choices.label: Humming while cooking
reply: Humming while cooking. Oh, how sweet.
The kitchen becomes a little concert.

choices.label: Talking to plants
reply: Talking to plants. Oh, how charming.
The ferns are listening.

A:A: Humming, and {partner} knew it.
Oh, they love the background music of your kitchen.
Keep humming. Never stop.
A:B: Plant chats for you. {partner} guessed humming.
Oh, dear, they think it's the humming. It's the ferns.
Tell them which plant is your favorite.
B:A: Humming for you. {partner} guessed plant chats.
Well, they think it's the plants. It's the humming.
Hum to the plants. Double charm.
B:B: Talking to plants, and {partner} knew it.
Oh, they love how you say good morning to the ferns.
The ferns love it too, darling.

questions.scene: Duchess pulls a leather notebook from her bag. 'My memoir,' she whispers.
lines: Oh, dear, if love were a book...
questions.question: If your partner wrote your love story, what genre would it be?
questions.selfQuestion: If you wrote your love story, what genre would it be?

choices.label: Cozy romance
reply: Cozy romance. Oh, how lovely.
Candlelight, rain, and tea.

choices.label: Comedy of errors
reply: Comedy of errors. Oh, how fun!
Chaos and laughter, chapter after chapter.

A:A: Cozy romance, and {partner} knew it.
Oh, they'd write chapter after chapter of cuddles.
A bestseller, I'm sure.
A:B: Comedy for you. {partner} guessed cozy romance.
They think it's all candles. You remember the chaos.
Both are true. That's the secret of 40 years.
B:A: Cozy romance for you. {partner} guessed comedy.
They think you see the chaos. You see the candlelight.
Co-write it. Romance with a funny chapter.
B:B: Comedy of errors, and {partner} knew it.
Bless them, they'd include every disaster.
The best love stories are the funny ones.

questions.scene: Duchess gazes out the window, smiling at something far away.
lines: Forty years from now. Picture it, darling.
questions.question: Forty years from now, what will your partner still do every morning?
questions.selfQuestion: Forty years from now, what will you still do every morning?

choices.label: Make the tea for two
reply: Tea for two. Oh, how lovely.
A morning ritual for a lifetime.

choices.label: Steal all the blankets
reply: Steal the blankets. Oh, dear, a classic.
Some things never change.

A:A: Tea for two, and {partner} knew it.
Oh, a morning cup together forever.
Bartholomew makes mine. Forty years. Never missed one.
A:B: Blanket thief. {partner} guessed tea.
Well, they expected a warm cup. They got cold toes.
Make them tea as an apology. Every morning.
B:A: Tea for you. {partner} guessed blanket theft.
Ha! They think you're a thief. You're a tea maker.
Make the tea. Leave the blankets.
B:B: Blanket theft, and {partner} knew it.
Darling, they've accepted their fate.
Forty more years of cold toes. That's commitment.
